first.rationale: The concurrent declines in onboarding completion and activation make onboarding simplification the most directly evidenced, reversible lever for restoring early adoption. Promotional pricing addresses competitive pressure but has documented 30-day retention harm, which conflicts with sustainable qualified revenue. Verify the original onboarding records before committing to confirm segment applicability and guardrails.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding-simplification experiment focused on the self-serve/SMB path. Shortened onboarding has confirmed gains in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing both current declines. The SMB signup-simplification result also supports activation and qualified-revenue upside, but its 1% retention decline means retention and qualified revenue must be primary guardrails. Do not use broad promotional pricing: its known retention damage conflicts with the sustainable-revenue objective.

final2.rationale: Keep the guarded self-serve/SMB onboarding-simplification experiment. It directly addresses the observed declines in completion and activation, while shortened onboarding previously improved 30-day retention. The competitor's cut raises the urgency of the SMB problem, but the inherited pricing result shows that promotional pricing materially harmed 30-day retention; under a sustainable qualified-revenue objective, it should not displace the chosen experiment without new evidence that a narrowly targeted retention offer has acceptable downstream value.
